why: A (universes 0): for a slice submanifold N ⊆ V (any normed V, any finite-dimensional model Z) and F smooth on V, only LINEAR perturbations are controlled: ∃ δ, every critical point in K of (F + a)|N with a ∈ V* linear, ‖a‖ < δ, has index ≥ λ₀ (globally, and per slice chart near z₀). B (Milnor: 'g with first and second derivatives so close that Lemma 22.4 applies in a coordinate neighbourhood'): on an abstract smooth ℝᵐ-manifold, for any finite cover of K by compacts in charts, ∃ ε such that EVERY smooth g whose first and second chart partials are ε-close to f's has its critical points in K of index ≥ λ₀. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: linear perturbations of an ambient function are a small subclass of B's g (and abstract manifolds vs slice submanifolds). B ⇒ A fails only by the setting (A allows any model Z and any normed V): on the Bridge's ↥N (finite-dimensional inner-product V, Z = ℝⁿ) B gives A's global conjunct, proved (B_emb_to_A_emb). So on embedded manifolds A is the special case g = (F + a)|N of B.
